page.layout: Running head at top, with the page number at top left. Below it, two circular medallion portraits side by side, each with its inscription in the ring: left Lecapenus, right Romanus junior. Below them one text block of two paragraphs in one column. No notes in the margins, and no printed block under the text.

main_text.p: ROMANVS Lecapenus obscuro genere natus, insidias Constantino parauit, imperiique Constantinopolitani socius ac particeps ab eodem necessario adscitus est eodem quo regnare coepit Constantinus anno, uti supra videre est: Helenamque Constantini filiam, pulsa matre Zoë uxorem habuit. Nec tamen iusiurandum sanctissimum quod praestiterat Lecapenus nec gener Constantinus obstitit, quo minus imperium & sibi & Christophoro filio idem Lecapenus assereret. Cum autem aduersus Bulgaros, Simeonémque eorum ducem, infeliciter congressus esset, à Stephano & Constantino, filiis suis captus, imperio exuitur, & in vicinam insulam in monasterium ad Philosophandum relegatur. At cum iidem ipsi aduersus Constantinum Leonis filium idem molirentur, in laqueum quem tetenderant incidunt, nam & ipsimet, Lecapeni inquam filij, monasterio mancipantur. Imperauit Romanus Lecapenus annos 39. Vide Liuthprandum lib.5.ca.9.10. & 11. Egna.lib.2. Cosmog. Munst. lib.4.

ROMANVS Constantini, Leonis filij, filius iunior, post patrem imperium suscepit Constantinopolitanum, quod tamen alieno rexit arbitrio, nempe Nicephori Phocæ, de quo statim meminerimus, ubi & annorum supputationem inferam, non hic ne bis id faciam. Fuit Romanus hic foris aduersus Saracenos Cretam occupantes, & Turcas Asiam vastantes, Nicephori ductu felix: domi in matrem ac sorores impius, ut regia eiectæ, ob mærorem quòd regio essent exutæ vestitu, quæstum fecerint meretricium: ipse ludis ac crapulæ deditus, anno imperij decimo, veneno potionatur. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: The two medallions are woodcut portraits of Romanus Lecapenus (left, bearded, laureate, facing right) and Romanus junior (right, youthful, laureate, facing right); they are not transcribed as text. The marginal note "39. Vide..." stands in the left margin beside the words "annos" and is placed there in the transcription. Long s has been written as s throughout. Words broken at line ends without a printed hyphen (Phi-losophandum, teten-derant, Sara-cenos) are written whole.
